newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
SHARAD CAMP TARGETS GUJRAL

The battle between Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and his critics in the Janata Dal party is poised to escalate with the official camp in the party projecting former Prime Minister Deve Gowda as its leader. The two-day Janata Dal party convention ended in New Delhi on Sunday with the Sharad Yadav-Deve Gowda combine giving the party a distinctly anti-Congress stance. The Dal also asked former partymen to return to the party. The appeal, which was aimed at former party colleagues from Bihar state, made it clear that a reunification would be possible only under the presidentship of Sharad Yadav. The appeal was rejected by the Rashtriya Janata Dal party's Working President Ranjan Yadav.
The Times Of India
GOWDA DEMANDS BIHAR GOVERNMENT'S DISMISSAL

Chairman of the ruling United Front and former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda demanded the dismissal of the Bihar state government led by the Rashtriya Janata Dal party. Deve Gowda criticised the federal government for its helplessness in ending the government's rule in Bihar. Deve Gowda said the Janata Dal party had to strengthen itself, regardless of the presence of other United Front constituents or the Congress party. Gowda said his efforts to build the party organisation should not be interpreted as a bid to weaken the United Front government.
The Economic Times
FAST TRACK POLICIES ON TELECOM, POWER AND ROADS SOON

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said his government had identified roads, power and telecom sectors as growth areas and policies were being launched to give these sectors the required thrust. These areas are all fast-track ones and decisions will be taken to expedite implementation of projects, he said. The Cabinet Committee on Infrastructure recently decided to boost investment in these sectors. In the power sector, measures are being taken to upgrade existing facilities and ensure fuel supply.
FUND FOR AUTO ANCILLARY INDUSTRY BEING RAISED

The Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services (IL&FS) is setting up a fund for the auto ancillary industry. The Indian Auto Ancillary Fund will be the first of its kind for the industry. The Finance Ministry has given its consent to set up the fund. The International Finance Corporation, which is a private investment arm of the World Bank, has expressed its willingness to participate as a core investor in the fund. Subscription to the fund will be limited to leading institutional and wholesale investors, both offshore and domestic.
PIRELLI SPA SEEKS TELECOME VENTURE PARTNER

Italian tyre giant Pirelli SpA is entering Indian telecom and tyre sectors. Pirelli SpA plans to enter the telecom industry in India with its jelly-filled and fibre optic cables and systems. It has started exporting tyres to India through a Bombay-based tyre distributor who will sell the products through other retail outlets in all metros. It is initially looking towards the original equipment manufacturing market from the automobile manufacturers who are either exporting or planning to manufacture new generation vehicles. Pirelli has tied up with Birla Tyres to provide technology and know-how to set up a tyre manufacturing facility.
Financial Express
OVERSEAS COMPANY'S TO GET 100 PCT STAKE IN SMALL OILFIELDS

The ministries of petroleum and industry have agreed to allow 100 percent foreign equity in small discovered oilfields of national oil companies. But the foreign equity will be restricted to 60 percent for un-incorporated joint ventures and 51 percent for incorporated joint ventures for medium-sized fields. The new exploration and licensing policy will allow 100 percent foreign equity in new oil blocks that will be offered through a competitive bidding process in which national oil companies too can participate. The new policy proposal will soon be sent for cabinet approval.
TORRENT POWER PERMITTED TO GIVE SHARES TO OVERSEAS PARTNER

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) gave Torrent Power permission to issue preference shares worth four billion rupees to U.S.-based MCN Investment Corporation and its units. MCN is a partner of Torrent Power. The company and its subsidiaries will bring in capital. The proposal is now before the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment for final approval. Torrent Power will be the first company to issue preference shares to overseas investors after the Finance Ministry's recent decision to allow Indian companies to mobilise foreign investment by issuing preference shares.
Business Standard
INFLATION HITS RECORD LOW

The rate of inflation based on the wholesale price index touched an all-time low of 4.19 percent in the week ended July 19. When calculated on a point to point basis the rate of inflation fell by 0.24 percentage point from 4.43 percent a week earlier. It was 6.01 percent in the corresponding week last year. Since this June the rate of inflation has fallen by 1.74 percentage points.
SAVINGS RATE ROSE TO 25.8 PCT DURING LAST FISCAL

The average gross savings rate rose to 25.8 percent during fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) from 25.6 percent in fiscal 1995/96. Government sources predict a further increase of two percentage points in the rates during fiscal 1997/98. The incremental capital output ratio for the country has averaged around four percent in the last two decades. The Finance Ministry's target of seven percent Gross Domestic Product growth in 1997/98 now appears tenable.
The Observer
FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT IN TRADING UNDER REVIEW

The government is reviewing the policy on foreign direct investments in trading with a view to let in foreign trading firms in select high tech areas alone. A core group was set up to finalise the policy. The move follows widespread criticism of allowing foreign investments in an area (trading) which does not require any technological excellence. The government has decided to put on hold all foreign direct investment proposals for trading activities until it finalises the new policy. Under the existing policy, up to 100 percent foreign equity is allowed in trading activities in India. But they are allowed only in bulk trading and not in retailing.
